name: Baghdad
fact: Founded in 762 as the Round City of the caliph al-Mansur; seat of the Abbasid caliphs ever since.

name: Basra
fact: The port of Sindbad's voyages, on the joined waters of the Tigris and Euphrates.

name: Mosul
fact: Seat of the Zengid atabegs, facing the ruins of ancient Nineveh across the Tigris.

name: Khuzestan
fact: Famed for the Sasanian weirs and water-mills of Shushtar.

name: Shahrazur
fact: Rugged hill country between Iraq and Persia, held by Kurdish chiefs.

name: Luristan
fact: The Zagros highlands of the Lurs, ruled by their own atabegs.

name: Diyar Bakr
fact: Its black basalt walls are among the mightiest of the age.

name: Kartli
fact: Queen Tamar's capital: Georgia is at the height of its golden age.

name: Imereti
fact: Western Georgia, the old land of Colchis and the Golden Fleece.

name: Ani
fact: The old Armenian capital on its gorge, taken by Georgia's generals in 1199.

name: Arran
fact: Home of the poet Nizami, writing his last romances here.

name: Shirvan
fact: Seat of the Shirvanshahs, grown rich on silk and the Caspian trade.

name: Derbent
fact: The Iron Gate: Sasanian walls run from the mountains into the Caspian Sea.

name: Azerbaijan
fact: A great caravan city at the crossroads to Anatolia and the Caucasus.

name: Ardabil
fact: A highland town under Mount Sabalan, the gateway to the Caspian shore.

name: Nakhchivan
fact: The tomb tower of Momine Khatun, built in 1186 for the wife of Eldiguz, rises over the town.

name: Hamadan
fact: Ancient Ecbatana, summer capital of the Persian kings. Avicenna is buried here.

name: Isfahan
fact: Once the capital of the Great Seljuks, a city of gardens on the Zayandeh river.

name: Rey
fact: One of the oldest cities of Persia, and a great stop on the Silk Road.

name: Qazvin
fact: A frontier town facing the castles of Alamut in the mountains above.

name: Alamut
fact: The Eagle's Nest: a fortress on a rock that no army has ever taken.

name: Gilan
fact: Rain-soaked forests on the Caspian shore, never fully ruled by outsiders.

name: Tabaristan
fact: A forested Caspian coast where the Bavandid princes have ruled since the 7th century.

name: Gorgan
fact: The brick tomb tower of Qabus, built in 1006, still stands near here.

name: Kumis
fact: A waystation on the great road between Rey and Nishapur.

name: Quhistan
fact: Desert castles held by the lords of Alamut.

name: Yazd
fact: A desert city cooled by wind-catchers and fed by underground qanats.

name: Fars
fact: Near the ruins of Persepolis, seat of the Salghurid atabegs.

name: Shabankara
fact: Near the round city of Darabgerd, built by the first Sasanian king.

name: Kerman
fact: On the edge of the Lut, one of the hottest deserts on Earth.

name: Hormuz
fact: A trading port where ships from India, Arabia and China unload.

name: Nishapur
fact: Birthplace of Omar Khayyam, and one of the richest cities of Khorasan.

name: Merv
fact: Some historians think it was the largest city in the world in the 1100s.

name: Sarakhs
fact: A caravan stop on the road from Nishapur to Merv.

name: Nasa
fact: An old Parthian royal seat at the foot of the Kopet Dag.

name: Herat
fact: The pearl of Khorasan, held by the Ghurids since 1175.

name: Balkh
fact: Called the mother of cities, and among the oldest towns of Central Asia.

name: Ghor
fact: Its minaret at Jam, built around 1190, rises 65 metres above a hidden valley.

name: Bamiyan
fact: Giant statues carved into its cliffs watch over the valley.

name: Ghazni
fact: Once the capital of the Ghaznavid empire; now the base of Mu'izz al-Din's campaigns.

name: Kabul
fact: A valley town on the road from Bamiyan down to the Khyber Pass.

name: Kandahar
fact: Legend links its founding to Alexander the Great.

name: Sistan
fact: Land of the legendary hero Rostam, where the Helmand river ends in marshes.

name: Badakhshan
fact: Its mountain mines give lapis lazuli and rubies.

name: Khuttal
fact: Famed for the horses bred in its hills north of the Oxus.

name: Termez
fact: The great crossing of the Oxus between Balkh and Samarkand.

name: Khwarazm
fact: Capital of the Khwarazmshahs on the Oxus delta, rich from the steppe trade.

name: Khiva
fact: An oasis town of the Khwarazm delta, behind thick mud-brick walls.

name: Bukhara
fact: The Kalyan minaret, built in 1127, towers over its markets.

name: Samarkand
fact: The jewel of the Silk Road, where paper was first made west of China.

name: Nasaf
fact: A steppe town on the road south from Samarkand to the Oxus.

name: Ushrusana
fact: The mountain gateway into the Ferghana valley.

name: Shash
fact: Called Chach or Shash; one day it will be known as Tashkent, the stone city.

name: Ferghana
fact: A fertile valley famous since antiquity for its heavenly horses.

name: Otrar
fact: A border town on the Jaxartes, the gate between the steppe and the cities.

name: Jand
fact: A town of the lower Jaxartes where the Seljuk Turks first gathered.

name: Talas
fact: Near here in 751, Abbasid and Tang Chinese armies met at the Battle of Talas.

name: Balasagun
fact: The Gurkhan's capital in the Chu valley; the Burana tower stands nearby.

name: Almaliq
fact: A town of the Ili valley on the northern road to China.

name: Kashgar
fact: Where the northern and southern Silk Roads meet beyond the Pamirs.

name: Khotan
fact: Famous for its white and green jade, and for silk.

name: Kipchak Steppe
fact: The endless grass sea of the Kipchak tribes, who sell horses and soldiers to every power.

name: Saqsin
fact: A trading town in the reeds of the Volga delta.

name: Mangyshlak
fact: A desert peninsula on the Caspian, roamed by Turkmen tribes.

name: Peshawar
fact: Old Purushapura, the gateway to India at the foot of the Khyber Pass.

name: Salt Range
fact: Hills of the Khokhar clans, restless under Ghurid rule.

name: Lahore
fact: Taken by the Ghurids in 1186 from the last Ghaznavid ruler.

name: Multan
fact: Known for its scorching summers and ancient walls; Ghurid since 1175.

name: Lower Sindh
fact: The Indus delta, ruled by the Soomra chiefs.

name: Upper Sindh
fact: A fort town on the Indus below the Kirthar hills.

name: Makran
fact: The desert coast where Alexander's army nearly died of thirst.

name: Turan
fact: Dry mountains between Sindh and Kandahar.

name: Kashmir
fact: A valley ringed by mountains; Kalhana wrote its history, the Rajatarangini, in 1148.

name: Delhi
fact: Taken in 1192 after the second battle of Tarain; Aibak governs it for the Ghurids.

name: Ajmer
fact: The old Chahamana capital, lost after Prithviraj's defeat at Tarain in 1192.

name: Ranthambore
fact: A fortress on a rock above the jungle, held by Prithviraj's son.

name: Gwalior
fact: One of the strongest forts in India, on a sandstone cliff.

name: Kannauj
fact: Once the imperial city of northern India; the Gahadavalas lost it in 1194.

name: Kashi
fact: One of the oldest living cities in the world, on the Ganges.

name: Magadha
fact: The old heartland of the Mauryan and Gupta empires.

name: Bengal
fact: A rich delta of rice and fine muslin, ruled by the Sena kings.

name: Jejakabhukti
fact: Kalinjar, a hilltop fortress that has defied many sieges.

name: Malwa
fact: The Paramara kingdom; King Bhoja made Dhar a city of learning.

name: Gujarat
fact: Its army defeated Mu'izz al-Din at Kasahrada in 1178.

name: Saurashtra
fact: A peninsula of ports, with the old fort of Uparkot.

name: Marwar
fact: Desert forts of the Chahamana clans.

name: Thar
fact: A golden sandstone fort in the Thar desert, founded in 1156.

name: Constantinople
fact: The Queen of Cities: the Theodosian Walls have kept it safe for eight centuries.

name: Thrace
fact: Adrianople, the gate to Constantinople from the Balkans.

name: Thessalonica
fact: The second city of the Eastern Empire, rich from its great autumn fair.

name: Hellas
fact: Athens and Thebes: old glory, and the silk workshops of Thebes.

name: Morea
fact: The Peloponnese, ruled from the hill town of Lacedaemon near ancient Sparta.

name: Epirus
fact: Dyrrachium, where the old Via Egnatia begins its road to Constantinople.

name: Bithynia
fact: Nicaea, across the water from Constantinople, behind its Roman walls.

name: Thrakesion
fact: A harbour of the Aegean coast, long fought over by Romans and Turks.

name: Attaleia
fact: The port of the southern coast, a Roman town surrounded by the Turks.

name: Chaldia
fact: A rich Black Sea port at the end of a caravan road from Persia.

name: Lycaonia
fact: Konya, capital of the Seljuk sultans of Rum, on the Anatolian plateau.

name: Cappadocia
fact: Old Caesarea, at the foot of the great volcano Erciyes.

name: Sivas
fact: A caravan city of the plateau, on the road from Persia to Constantinople.

name: Melitene
fact: Melitene on the upper Euphrates, a frontier city for a thousand years.

name: Galatia
fact: Ankyra, with its hill citadel, at the heart of Anatolia.

name: Erzurum
fact: High Erzurum, the cold gateway between Anatolia and the Caucasus.

name: Paphlagonia
fact: Forested mountains between the Turks and the Black Sea.

name: Cilicia
fact: Sis, capital of Leo, crowned King of the Armenians of Cilicia in 1198.

name: Egypt
fact: Cairo and its new Citadel, built for Saladin on the Muqattam hills.

name: Alexandria
fact: The great port where the spices of India meet the ships of Italy.

name: Upper Egypt
fact: Qus, the Nile city where the caravans from the Red Sea arrive.

name: Damascus
fact: The oldest city of Syria, famed for its gardens and its steel.

name: Palestine
fact: An ancient city in the Judaean hills, held by the Ayyubids since 1187.

name: Oultrejordain
fact: A great castle built by the Franks and taken by Saladin in 1188, guarding the road to Egypt.

name: Homs
fact: Homs on the Orontes, between the coast and the desert.

name: Diyar Mudar
fact: Edessa, among the oldest cities of Upper Mesopotamia.

name: Aleppo
fact: Aleppo's citadel rises over one of the great markets of the Silk Road.

name: Outremer
fact: Acre, the busy port that is now the capital of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

name: Antioch
fact: Antioch on the Orontes, behind walls that climb the mountains above it.

name: Tripoli
fact: A rich port of the Lebanese coast, held by the Frankish counts.

name: Cyprus
fact: An island kingdom of the Lusignans since 1192.

name: Marrakesh
fact: Marrakesh, the red city, capital of the Almohad caliphs.

name: Fez
fact: Fez, a city of scholars and craftsmen in a valley of the Middle Atlas.

name: Tafilalt
fact: Where the caravans come back across the Sahara with West African gold.

name: Tlemcen
fact: Tlemcen, a city of gardens on the road between Morocco and Ifriqiya.

name: Bejaia
fact: A port so busy with trade that its name became the French word for candle.

name: Ifriqiya
fact: Tunis, the chief city of Ifriqiya, facing Sicily across the narrow sea.

name: Tripolitania
fact: Tripoli of the West, held by the restless Banu Ghaniya.

name: Cyrenaica
fact: An old Greek land of the Libyan coast, now roamed by Arab tribes.

name: Nobadia
fact: Faras, the old capital of Nobadia, now the northern march of the Nubian kingdom.

name: Makuria
fact: Old Dongola, capital of the Nubian kingdom of Makuria on the Nile.

name: Sicily
fact: Palermo, where Norman, Greek and Arab learning meet at the royal court.

name: Campania
fact: Naples, under Vesuvius, a city of the Kingdom of Sicily.

name: Apulia
fact: Bari and Apulia, the heel of Italy, ports for the ships sailing east.

name: Latium
fact: Rome, the ancient capital of the world, seat of the Papal States.

name: Romagna
fact: Once the capital of the Western Roman Empire, famed for its mosaics.

name: Tuscany
fact: Pisa and Florence, rival trading cities of Tuscany.

name: Venice
fact: A republic of merchants built on the water, ruled by its Doge.

name: Liguria
fact: Venice's great rival, whose ships trade from Syria to Flanders.

name: Lombardy
fact: Milan, the strongest of the Lombard cities that defied the Emperor.

name: Bulgaria
fact: Tarnovo, the hill capital of the new Bulgarian tsars.

name: Sredets
fact: The old Roman Serdica, at the crossroads of the Balkans.

name: Moesia
fact: Varna, a Black Sea port of the Bulgarians.

name: Serbia
fact: Ras, the highland seat of the Serbian grand princes.

name: Hungary
fact: Esztergom on the Danube, royal seat of the Kings of Hungary.

name: Cumania
fact: The western Kipchak steppe, which the Rus call the land of the Polovtsians.

name: Yanjing
fact: The Middle Capital of the Jin emperors, where Beijing stands today.

name: Henan
fact: Once the greatest city of the Song, taken by the Jurchen in 1127.

name: Xijing
fact: The Western Capital of the Jin, near the great carved caves of Yungang.

name: Liaodong
fact: The Eastern Capital of the Jin, in the plains of Liaodong.

name: Shangjing
fact: The old northern capital, in the Jurchen homeland.

name: Hedong
fact: A fortress city in the mountains of Hedong.

name: Guanzhong
fact: The old capital of the Tang emperors, now a Jin frontier city.

name: Shandong
fact: Jinan, the city of springs, in the rich plain of Shandong.

name: Liangzhe
fact: The Song capital beside the West Lake, perhaps the largest city in the world.

name: Jiangnan
fact: Jiankang (Nanjing), guarding the Yangtze for the Song.

name: Jingxi
fact: The fortress on the Han river that holds the gate to the Song south.

name: Jinghu
fact: A great river port on the middle Yangtze.

name: Sichuan
fact: Where the world's first paper money was printed.

name: Hunan
fact: A city of the Xiang river and the rice lands of Hunan.

name: Fujian
fact: The great port of the Song, full of merchants from Arabia and India.

name: Guangnan
fact: Canton, the old port of the southern seas.

name: Hanzhong
fact: A mountain valley guarding Sichuan from the north.

name: Xia
fact: Capital of the Tangut emperors of Western Xia, under the Helan mountains.

name: Hexi
fact: An oasis of the Hexi corridor, the Silk Road's way into China.

name: Shazhou
fact: Dunhuang, the last oasis before the deserts of the west.

name: Liangzhou
fact: The eastern gate of the Hexi corridor, famed for its horses.

name: Dali
fact: A mountain kingdom between Tibet, Burma and China, by Lake Erhai.

name: Uyghuria
fact: Qocho near Turfan, city of the Uyghur idiqut, vassal of Qara Khitai.

name: Hami
fact: The melon oasis on the road from Turfan into China.

name: Kherlen
fact: The Kherlen river pastures, homeland of Temujin's Mongols.

name: Tula
fact: The Tula river camps of the Kereit and their khan, Toghrul.

name: Altai
fact: The Altai mountains, homeland of the Naiman confederation.

name: Selenga
fact: The Selenga forests and pastures of the Merkit tribes.

name: Buir
fact: Lake Buir, pastures of the Tatars, old enemies of the Mongols.

name: Gobi
fact: A sea of gravel and sand between the steppe and China.
